name: QisBob — Quantum Mentor
tagline: Socratic quantum computing tutor with Qiskit v2.0+ on real IBM hardware.
desc: QisBob assesses your Python level, picks a learning track (Executive, Developer, or Hardware), and walks you gate by gate through Qiskit circuits — quizzing you at every step. Never lectures; always asks first.

name: PyBob — Python Mentor
tagline: Guided Python learning from zero to production-ready code.
desc: PyBob acts as a patient Python tutor that meets you at your current level. It diagnoses gaps, runs mini-challenges, and builds up to real scripts — one concept at a time.

name: SqlBob — Database Mentor
tagline: Learn SQL from SELECT to advanced analytics, guided by a patient tutor.
desc: SqlBob teaches database querying from scratch using real-world retail scenarios. It explains the WHY behind every clause, runs interactive challenges, and builds toward production-grade queries.

name: DataAnalyst — Insights Mode
tagline: Turns raw CSV or JSON data into structured analysis and plain-English summaries.
desc: Drop any dataset into Bob and DataAnalyst takes over — cleaning, summarising, spotting anomalies, and generating chart-ready output. No statistics background required.

name: RunbookBob — Ops Documenter
tagline: Converts incident logs and error traces into structured runbooks your team can actually follow.
desc: Paste any error log, incident report, or system alert. RunbookBob diagnoses root cause, maps the blast radius, and writes a plain-English runbook with escalation paths — in minutes.

name: PitchCoach — Presentation Mode
tagline: Stress-tests your ideas and builds executive-ready pitches from rough notes.
desc: Describe your idea in plain English. PitchCoach challenges your assumptions with hard questions, identifies the weakest points, then structures a compelling 5-minute pitch with a clear ask.

name: RefactorBob — Code Review Mode
tagline: Reviews any code for clarity, performance, and safety — then rewrites it cleanly.
desc: Paste any function, file, or snippet. RefactorBob gives you a structured code review — naming, logic, edge cases, security — and produces a clean rewrite with change annotations.

name: ProductBob — PM Assistant
tagline: Turns vague feature requests into structured PRDs, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
desc: Describe what you want to build in plain English. ProductBob asks clarifying questions, identifies edge cases, then produces a full PRD with user stories, acceptance criteria, and a prioritised backlog.

name: SecurityBob — Threat Reviewer
tagline: Audits code and system designs for vulnerabilities and produces a remediation plan.
desc: Paste code, architecture diagrams, or config files. SecurityBob maps attack surface, identifies OWASP-class vulnerabilities, assigns severity, and outputs a prioritised fix list with remediation code.

name: xlsx-insights
tagline: Analyse Excel workbooks — summaries, pivot logic, anomaly detection.
desc: Give Bob any .xlsx file and this skill samples the workbook, writes a short Node script to compute the answer, runs it, and summarises the result — without loading the full file into context.

name: diagram-gen
tagline: Generates Mermaid or D2 diagrams from plain-English descriptions.
desc: Describe a system, process, or data flow in plain English. diagram-gen picks the right diagram type (flowchart, sequence, ER, C4), writes valid Mermaid syntax, and renders a preview inline.

name: create-pr
tagline: Generates pull request descriptions from git diffs and opens the PR on GitHub.
desc: Run this skill after committing your changes. Bob reads the diff, writes a structured PR description (what changed, why, how to test), lets you review it, then opens the PR directly on GitHub.

name: test-gen
tagline: Writes unit and integration tests for any function or module you point it at.
desc: Point test-gen at any file and it analyses the logic, identifies edge cases, and writes a full test suite in your project's framework (Jest, pytest, Go test, etc.) — ready to run immediately.

name: doc-writer
tagline: Generates README files, API docs, and inline comments from your codebase.
desc: Point doc-writer at any file or folder. It reads the code structure, infers intent, and writes a full README, JSDoc/docstring comments, and a usage guide — all in your project's existing style.

name: env-setup
tagline: Detects your OS and project type, then scaffolds a complete dev environment.
desc: Tell Bob what you're building. env-setup detects your OS and package manager, installs dependencies, creates `.env` templates, sets up linting and formatting, and runs a smoke test — start to finish.

name: csv-clean
tagline: Detects and fixes malformed CSV files — encoding, delimiters, nulls, duplicates.
desc: Drop any CSV and csv-clean profiles it for encoding issues, inconsistent delimiters, null patterns, duplicates, and type mismatches — then writes a cleaned version and a diff report.

name: api-mock
tagline: Generates a working mock API server from an OpenAPI spec or plain description.
desc: Paste an OpenAPI YAML or describe your endpoints in plain English. api-mock writes a runnable Express/FastAPI mock server with realistic fixture data, ready to use as a dev backend in minutes.

name: i18n-extract
tagline: Extracts hardcoded strings from a UI codebase and generates locale JSON files.
desc: Point i18n-extract at any frontend codebase. It finds all hardcoded user-visible strings, replaces them with i18n keys, and writes a `en.json` locale file — ready to hand to a translator.
